fidelity_receipt.changed_predicate: a pixel counts as changed when its RGBA value in the composite differs at all from the stored foreground at a position where the foreground alpha equals opaque_alpha_threshold; edge-band pixels (0 < alpha < threshold) blend by design, are excluded from the count, and are published above as edge_band_pixels and edge_band_max_width_px
fidelity_receipt.claim: The stored extracted foreground reached the composite unchanged: every fully opaque foreground pixel in the composite is identical to the stored foreground layer (foreground hashes above pin that layer). Edge-band pixels blend with the plate by design and are counted separately. The composite carries the source photo's colour profile unchanged (color_profile_preserved above); a profile change is a fidelity failure even when pixel values match.

provenance.scope: Observations about what the file itself contains and claims, read when the photo arrived. These are not a verdict: this record never calls a photo edited or unedited. Metadata is written by software and can be edited or stripped, so the absence of any signal below is not evidence that a file is untouched.

signals.detail: the file names its capture device as Apple iPhone 17 Pro
signals.does_not_establish: metadata is written by software and can be edited or stripped, so a named device does not prove the photo came from that device
signals.establishes: the file's own statement of what captured it

signals.detail: no editing software is named anywhere in the file's metadata
signals.does_not_establish: silence is not cleanliness: an edited file whose metadata was stripped reads exactly like this, so this line can never clear a file
signals.establishes: nothing; this is the expected state of an untouched camera file

signals.detail: no edit history is recorded in the file
signals.does_not_establish: an edit history appears only when Adobe-family tools wrote one and the packet survived; its absence says nothing about edits by other tools or after a strip
signals.establishes: nothing; most camera files carry no history packet at all

signals.detail: no XMP document identifiers are present
signals.does_not_establish: identifiers speak only to whether copies can be recognised as related; their absence is the normal state of camera files

signals.detail: the file's modification date and stated capture time agree (2026:10:31 16:43:27)
signals.does_not_establish: agreement is easy to preserve or to fake, and exports often rewrite both together; this line can never clear a file
signals.establishes: the file's two dates tell one consistent story

signals.detail: no Content Credentials (C2PA) manifest is embedded. Most cameras add none, and no native iPhone photo carries one, so this absence means nothing
signals.does_not_establish: absence must never be read as suspicion: the large majority of unedited photos on earth carry no credential
signals.establishes: nothing; absence of credentials is the normal state of most honest photos

signals.detail: the metadata states 5712x4284 and the decoded image matches (orientation may swap the pair)
signals.does_not_establish: agreement is the normal state of untouched and competently exported files alike
signals.establishes: the file's description of its size agrees with the image it contains

signals.does_not_establish: a clean ending says nothing about the image data itself
signals.establishes: the file ends where its structure says it ends
